proposal.observation: Round 1 was rejected: score 0.6592 to 0.6460, correspondence_f1@15 0.364 to 0.343, sam_fill_rate essentially unchanged (0.729 to 0.728), ring_count_error still 0, depth_nan_ratio 0.131 to 0.135. The rejected overlay lowered curvature_threshold, binary_threshold and hough_threshold_oblique, raised maxLineGap_oblique and hough_threshold_horizontal, and set uniform_k_snap false. After that, the two oblique tracks (green negative-angle, red positive-angle) still sit beside the centre seam and still fade on the sparse right, but the left columns gained extra stray green and red segments. Prompt Y did not follow the track slope: seven rings are midpoints already at about 1550 and the three right rings are assumes at the same row. The start prompts were already a flat propagated row at that design Y, so the snap was not the correspondence error. Stage 1 stays locked.
proposal.rule: If relaxing oblique and binary thresholds, widening maxLineGap, and disabling uniform_k_snap lowers correspondence while measured prompt Y is already on the design row, the next overlay must tighten line acceptance and keep the snap. Do not retune unfolding or the vertical Hough threshold.
proposal.rationale: Correspondence is line pixels versus SAM block boundaries at 15 px. Round 1 added unexplained oblique fragments and lost 0.021 F1, so the start is precision-limited, not recall-limited. Raise curvature_threshold from 0.0005 to 0.0008 so only sharper joints reach the edge map (the lower value also nudged depth_nan up). Raise binary_threshold from 127 to 136 and hough_threshold_oblique from 30 to 36 so the K-edge tracks, which sit on the bright seams, survive while the short left-column fragments do not. Raise hough_threshold_horizontal from 30 to 50 to drop the isolated blue horizontals, which are outside the 4-10 deg taper window. Leave maxLineGap_oblique at 30, uniform_k_snap true, hough_threshold_vertical at 1500, and SAM geometry untouched: the template is already placing ten rings and a 0.729 fill, and the worked full overlays that moved those knobs jointly cut fill and correspondence.
